26 June — 28 July

Hamari Kahani

One month. Every day of it, in order, exactly as it happened.
Before you go — I wanted you to see it the way I remember it.

26th June · Friday

The first call.

We hadn't even met, and somehow we talked for hours. I remember hanging up and realising I'd been smiling at nothing for the last twenty minutes. I didn't know it yet, but that was the night everything started.

Day 2

You said good people don't exist.
I stayed on the phone until you believed otherwise.

You told me you'd stopped expecting kindness from people — that you'd been let down enough times to stop believing good ones were out there. I didn't try to convince you with words. I just kept showing up, one conversation at a time, until you didn't need convincing anymore.

Two weeks in

The first time I saw you.

Two weeks of voice notes and late-night calls, and then finally, a face to go with the voice I already knew by heart. I remember exactly what you were wearing. I remember not knowing what to say for the first few seconds.

10th July

The day I wrote you a letter.

We'd had our first real disagreement, and instead of just texting it out, I sat down and wrote you something by hand — the first time I'd ever done that for anyone. It felt like the only honest way to say what I meant.

The call where we decided

You cried. I did too, right after I hung up.

We both knew this day was coming — we just didn't know it would hurt this much when it actually arrived. Hearing you cry on that call broke something in me that I still haven't fully put back together. I didn't want to let you go. I still don't. But I understood why we had to talk about it.

Last week

I'm sorry for how I behaved.

We fought, and I said things — or maybe just said them in the wrong way — that hurt you when you were already carrying enough. That's not who I want to be with you, especially not now. I'm sorry. It doesn't erase it, but I need you to know I mean it: you didn't deserve to be spoken to that way, not by me, not by anyone.

Even that fight is part of us though — every couple has one they wish they could take back. I'd rather it exist and be owned than be pretended away.

Today · 28th July

The last day.

Whatever happens after this — however long "for now" turns out to be — I needed you to have this. Not a message that disappears, something that stays. Go finish what you set out to do. I'll be one of the people quietly hoping you get there.

Zaroori Tha — Rahat Fateh Ali Khan
